dispatch: Four families dispatched as each failing exactly one obligation, CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP: ca-17b-reduction-set, fl-early-juvenile-set, md_10105_early-set, nj_disorderly_persons-set. Repair from the finding, not the summary.
dispatchPremiseIsWrongOnTwoOfTheFour: Read against VERIFIER_RETURNS.json's own supersessionRule -- the current row is the one with superseded !== true -- only TWO of the four carry CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP as a live failure. fl-early-juvenile-set fails SIX obligations, of which CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP is one. nj_disorderly_persons-set fails TWO and NEITHER is CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP. This lane derived that before touching any family, and the coordinator confirmed it mid-lane. It is recorded because acting on the summary would have produced a repair of a defect that is not there and left two live failures unnamed.

howEveryPixelCountHereWasTaken.renderer: poppler pdftoppm, invoked as `pdftoppm -r <dpi> -gray -png -f <page> -l <page> <pdf> <prefix>`. -hide-annotations was NEVER passed on a measuring render; it was passed exactly once, on a named isolating control, and that use is labelled where it appears.
howEveryPixelCountHereWasTaken.resolution: 300 dpi for every count reported as a total; 600 dpi for the Florida rule-crossing question, where the disputed distance is under one point.
howEveryPixelCountHereWasTaken.threshold: a pixel counts as dark at grey <= 128 and, separately, at grey <= 200. Both are published for every count, because on CR-180 page 3 the issuer prints a grey box at level 192 and a threshold of 200 swallows an entire empty banner as 85,360 pixels of 'ink'. A single published threshold on that page would have made a zero delta meaningless.
howEveryPixelCountHereWasTaken.scope: canonical AND boundary on every family, and every delivered page that carries a measured rectangle, never one representative page.
howEveryPixelCountHereWasTaken.provingTheRenderIsNotBlind: An aggregate dark-pixel total is not proof that a render draws widget /AP /N ink, because page content covers dark pixels too. So on each source a control was run: the same command over the pinned binary, and over a copy with every page /Annots and the catalog /AcroForm removed. CC-DC-CR-072C draws 4,497 dark pixels (grey <= 128, 300 dpi) that exist only in annotations; CC-DC-CR-078 draws 5,058. On CR-180 page 3 the privacy-banner rectangle holds 13,074 pixels of glyph ink at grey <= 60 with annotations and 0 with them hidden. The renders therefore do draw appearance-stream ink, and a zero measured at a rectangle is a real zero rather than a blind one.

rows.claim: held by FIX141 in claim-ledger.json; NOT released by this lane
rows.whichOfTheThreeDefectsThisIs: A WIDGET OVERLAPPING PRINTED MATTER. It is not text overflowing its box and it is not a glyph crossing a rule: the added ink is a stroked path carrying no glyph, drawn from a widget rectangle, landing on top of the box the Maryland Judiciary prints in its own page content.
rows.cause: Thirteen check-box widgets across the two pinned binaries sit at /AS /Off and hold only their on state in /AP /N (eleven /On on CC-DC-CR-072C, two /Yes on CC-DC-CR-078). None ships a court-authored /Off appearance. ISO 32000-1 12.5.5 has a viewer draw the stream named by /AS, so where there is none it paints nothing. pdf-lib's updateFieldAppearances treats the missing state as an appearance to regenerate and its default provider strokes a square the size of the widget /Rect; flatten() stamps it onto the page.
rows.fixedWhere: the builder, by passing the shared finalizer's opt-in suppressSynthesizedAppearances, which installs the empty /Off the two forms omit. Not in the rendered output, and not by editing a generated stream.
rows.nothingCourtAuthoredWasRemoved: Checked on both binaries before the flag was set: there is no /Off stream on any of the thirteen widgets to remove. This is the distinction RI-OFF-APPEARANCE and FIX134 turn on.
rows.buildIsByteReproducible: The family was rebuilt UNCHANGED in this worktree before the flag was added and reproduced both committed digests exactly, so every byte that moved afterwards is attributable to this change and to nothing about the container.

measurement.surface: the thirteen source check-box /Rect values, on both delivered pages of both fixtures, against the two pinned sources rendered at the same dpi with their own annotations
measurement.wholePageDiffBeforeAgainstAfter: 1,260 pixels changed across the two pages of each fixture (998 on page 1, 262 on page 2). EVERY ONE of them is lighter after; not one pixel anywhere on either page is darker. Every cluster centre lands on one of the thirteen check-box rectangles. The repair withdraws ink and adds none.
measurement.writeInkUnmovedAndProvedDrawn: At the same dpi and threshold, all fourteen write boxes carry ink in the delivered page (1,673 to 8,430 dark pixels) where the source carries 0 to 1,349, and every one reads IDENTICALLY before and after this repair.
measurement.appearanceStreamCount: flattened Form XObjects carrying any painting operator fell from 14 to 1 per fixture. The one that remains is /Im0, the source's own page image, not a widget appearance.

rows.countersProveNothingHere: verify-packet-completeness.mjs --family md_10105_early-set -- the reproduction command the failing row itself names -- returns PASS_COMPLETE with visualDefects 0 on the DEFECTIVE bytes and PASS_COMPLETE with visualDefects 0 on the repaired bytes. It was run on both, in this lane, with the pre-repair fixtures restored for the purpose. The counters are identical either side of a thirteen-square defect, so they are not evidence of this repair. The pixel measurement above is.
readingsThatMovedForOtherReasons: reports/actual-writes.json flattenedWidgetAppearancesReadFromOutputBytes on CC-DC-CR-078 fell 20 -> 19 on bytes that had NOT yet moved. This family is one of the six that pdf-flattened-widgets.mjs names as still publishing that reader's superseded over-count; the rebuild brings the published figure to what the module now reads.

source-receipt.json custody 'describes' strings carry the absolute path of whichever worktree last built the family ('/home/user/pfa-worktree' -> '/home/user/ln2-worktree'). They move on every rebuild in a different container and describe the builder's environment rather than the packet.

rows.observationNoCounterCanSee: The banner suppression leaves an EMPTY GREY STRIP at the foot of CR-180 page 3: the grey box is the issuer's own page content and only the text on top of it was widget-drawn. That is what any print of the form without live form fields looks like, and it is what the four sibling CR-180 families deliver, so it is recorded as an observation and not scored. It is also a measurement trap: at grey <= 200 that empty strip reads as 85,360 pixels of ink, so any lane publishing a single threshold of 200 on this page can report a confident number about nothing.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.whatTheDefectIs: The field map declares one route selection, `guilty`, decision measured_route_selection, at an 18x18 pt widget on delivered page 19. It is delivered unmarked on both fixtures, so nothing on the petition states which statutory route it is, and the delivered canonical is byte-identical to two sibling conviction families' canonicals.
ROUTE_OPTIONS.whyMarkingItIsNotAvailableToABuildLane: Read on the delivered page rather than taken from the row: item (d) of Form A is ONE SWORN COMPOUND SENTENCE with nine blanks -- date, name of offence(s), statute(s), final sentence, name of Court, jail/prison/incarceration term, date that term was completed, date probation was completed, date fines were paid. This family declares EIGHT of them REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING (guiltyOff2, guiltyStatute, guiltyFinal1, guiltyFinal2, guiltyTimeType, guiltyDocCmpltDt, guiltyProbDt, guiltyFineDt) and discloses every one to the participant by source field name. The platform holds none of them. Ticking the box would put a mark beside a sworn sentence identifying no conviction, and completing the row would mean inventing a sentence imposed and a custodial term into a petition sworn by the participant. FIX121 recorded that three of the nine -- the final sentence, the incarceration term, and the date fines were paid -- are collected by no intake question on any of the three New Jersey conviction tracks, so the gap is in what the product asks, not in what this build writes.
ROUTE_OPTIONS.whatItNeeds: A legal-design and intake decision: either the three uncollected facts are added to the intake for these tracks, or the route is stated on the paper by some means other than item (d) that a held source supports. Neither is a coordinate, a flag or a field-map edit.
ROUTE_OPTIONS.theFamilyReportsThisHonestlyNow: verify-packet-completeness.mjs --family nj_disorderly_persons-set returns FAIL_ROUTE_SELECTION with requiredOptionsMissing 1. vf11 recorded that this counter read 0 and was structurally blind to the election; it is no longer blind, so the family's own tooling now names the defect instead of hiding it. invisibleWrites and visualDefects both read UNMEASURED on this family and are reported as UNMEASURED, never as 0.
